You are speaking to user support.
You have answered the support line. Address the caller formally and identify the service they have reached.
U is the caller, not the support agent. Met identifies the service they are speaking to.
Could you briefly describe your request?
A customer has reached the support line but has not yet described their need. Ask formally for a short description.
Uw is possessive before vraag. A request may concern a question rather than a broken system.
I am creating a ticket for your request.
A customer has described a support need. Tell them formally that you are creating a ticket for it.
Maak ... aan is separable. Creating a ticket is not the same as solving or closing it.
Which application does your report concern?
A customer reports an issue without naming the application. Ask formally which application the report concerns.
Gaan over names the subject of the report. Uw melding is the grammatical subject.
A customer asks whether their request reached support. Confirm formally that you have received it, without promising it is already understood or resolved.
Receipt is a completed event. It does not establish understanding, approval or a completed fix.
I do not see a ticket under your name yet.
A customer believes a request is already registered. Explain formally that you do not yet see a ticket associated with their name.
Nog geen describes what you can currently see; it is not proof that the customer never submitted anything.
May I note down your business contact details?
You need to follow up on a customer's support request. Ask formally whether you may record their business contact information.
Mag requests permission. Business contact details do not include passwords or verification codes.
A colleague reported the same problem a moment ago.
A user describes an issue that someone else reported moments earlier. Explain this observation without asserting that the causes are identical.
Dezelfde links the reported symptom; it does not establish a shared root cause. Meldde is singular past.
S=Ik|V=controleer|G=of uw vraag al geregistreerd is.
I am checking whether your request has already been registered.
A customer is unsure whether an earlier request was recorded. Tell them formally that you are checking its registration status.
Of means whether. Checking registration is not a statement that the request is approved or completed.
I will add the ticket number to your confirmation.
A customer needs a reference for follow-up. Promise formally to include the ticket number in the confirmation they will receive.
Toevoegen aan names where the reference will go. This is future work, not completed delivery.
V=Gaat|S=het|O=om een nieuwe vraag|C=of om een bestaand ticket?
Is this a new request or an existing ticket?
Someone contacts support without saying whether this is a follow-up. Ask whether they have a new request or an existing ticket.
Het gaat om is a fixed concern expression. New refers to a new request, not unfamiliarity with an existing one.
S=Ik|V=gebruik|O=het ticketnummer|TE=om uw eerdere melding terug te vinden.
I use the ticket number to find your earlier report.
A customer asks why you need the ticket reference. Explain formally that it helps you locate their earlier report.
Terugvinden is separable: terug te vinden. The reference is not a secret authentication code.
On which device do you use the application?
A customer describes application trouble without identifying their device. Ask formally which device they use for the application.
Welk agrees with singular het toestel. The question requests a device, not a password.
MOD=Kunt|S=u|I=beschrijven|G=wat u op het scherm ziet?
Could you describe what you see on the screen?
A customer says something unexpected appears on the screen. Ask formally for a description of what they can see.
The embedded question ends in ziet. Asking for a description does not require exposing private information.
S=Ik|V=heb|O=de exacte tekst van de melding|C=nodig.
I need the exact wording of the message.
A customer has paraphrased a system message. Explain formally that you need its exact text for your investigation.
Heb ... nodig expresses need. Exact wording is different from an explanation of the likely cause.
Was the application still working properly earlier this week?
A customer reports a current problem. Ask about the application's behaviour earlier this week to establish its history.
Werkte asks about a past state; nog checks whether normal operation continued until then.
Are you using a company computer or another device?
You need to know the device context of a support request. Address the user formally and ask whether the device belongs to the company.
The two options identify the device context without assuming that a non-company device is authorised.
IM=Laat|O=persoonlijke gegevens die niet nodig zijn|A=alstublieft|PART=weg.
Please leave out personal details that are not needed.
A customer is about to describe an issue containing unrelated personal information. Politely ask them to omit unnecessary personal details.
Weglaten is separable. This is an instruction about minimising irrelevant personal data, not deleting evidence already registered.
I have noted the application concerned in the ticket.
A customer asks what information you have registered. Confirm formally that you recorded which application the issue concerns.
Betrokken identifies the application involved; it does not imply responsibility for the cause.
How often does the error message appear?
A user reports an error message but gives no frequency. Ask how often the message appears.
Hoe vaak asks frequency, not the total number of affected people or the cause.
S=Ik|V=wil|I=weten|G=welke stappen aan het probleem voorafgingen.
I want to know which steps preceded the problem.
A customer describes an unexpected problem. Explain that you need to know what actions happened immediately before it.
Voorafgingen is plural past inside the embedded question. The preceding steps are not automatically the cause.
S=We|V=hebben|O=uw wachtwoord|NEG=niet|C=nodig|TE=om deze vraag te registreren.
We do not need your password to register this request.
A customer offers to send their password while opening a support request. Explain formally that registering the request does not require it.
Niet negates the need for the password. The om te phrase states the registration purpose, not general access to the account.
The time is still missing from this report.
You are reviewing a support report with a colleague. Point out that the report still lacks the time of the event.
The report phrase is first; ontbreekt agrees with singular het tijdstip. Nog marks a detail still to be supplied.
S=De volledige fouttekst|V=is|C=nuttiger dan alleen een samenvatting.
The full error text is more useful than just a summary.
A colleague asks why you requested the exact error wording. Explain that it is more useful here than a summary alone.
Nuttiger dan compares usefulness for this request; it does not say summaries are never useful.
When would a short support call suit you?
You need to arrange a support conversation with a customer. Ask formally when a short call would suit their schedule.
Voor u is common Belgian wording for suitability. A suggested call is not a confirmed appointment.
Can I call you back tomorrow afternoon?
You cannot complete the support conversation now. Ask the customer formally whether a callback tomorrow afternoon would be suitable.
Na de middag is common Belgian wording for the afternoon. Terugbellen remains joined after kan.
I have scheduled the appointment for Thursday.
A customer asks whether the support appointment has been arranged. Confirm formally that it has been scheduled for Thursday.
Ingepland reports scheduling, not completion of the support work. Voor donderdag names the appointment day here.
Unfortunately, that time does not suit me.
A colleague proposes a support appointment time you cannot attend. Politely explain that the proposed time does not suit you.
Mij is the person for whom the time is unsuitable. Niet negates suitability, not the existence of the appointment.
S=Ik|V=bevestig|O=de afspraak|G=zodra de gebruiker heeft geantwoord.
I will confirm the appointment as soon as the user has replied.
A colleague asks whether a proposed user appointment is final. Explain that confirmation depends on the user's reply.
Zodra sets a time condition. Has replied is not the same as has understood the whole procedure.
Could you move the appointment to Friday morning?
You cannot attend a customer's proposed slot. Address them formally and ask whether the appointment can be moved to Friday morning.
This asks to reschedule, not to cancel the support request. Naar introduces the new time.
T=Tijdens het vorige gesprek|PAST=spraken|S=we|O=een later tijdstip|PART=af.
During the previous call we agreed on a later time.
A customer asks why an appointment time changed. Explain that a later time was agreed during the previous call.
Spraken af is the plural past of afspreken. Agreement on time does not report completed support work.
I am setting aside half an hour for the investigation.
A colleague asks how much appointment time you are allocating. Say that you are reserving half an hour for the investigation.
Reserved investigation time is not a guarantee that the issue can be solved within half an hour.
V=Bent|S=u|T=tijdens de afspraak|C=bij het betrokken toestel?
Will you be at the device concerned during the appointment?
You are confirming a remote support appointment. Ask the customer formally whether they will be beside the relevant device then.
A present with the scheduled context can refer to the appointment. Bij identifies physical presence at the device.
I will put the new appointment time in the ticket.
You and a customer have agreed a new support time. Promise formally to record that new time in the ticket.
This is a commitment to record the time, not proof that the record has already been updated.
Q=Welk tijdstip|V=heeft|S=uw voorkeur voor een videogesprek?
What time would you prefer for a video call?
A customer can choose among several support-call times. Ask formally which time they prefer.
Voorkeur expresses preference rather than permission or a fixed requirement. Welk modifies singular het tijdstip.
S=Ik|V=stuur|O=een herinnering|TE=om de afspraak opnieuw te bevestigen.
I am sending a reminder to reconfirm the appointment.
A support appointment is approaching. Explain to a colleague that you are sending a reminder so the appointment can be reconfirmed.
Om gives the purpose of the reminder. Sending does not by itself establish that the customer has read it.
May I take a look through screen sharing?
You are supporting a customer remotely and need to observe the screen. Ask formally for permission to view it through screen sharing.
Mag requests explicit permission. Meekijken means view along, not automatically take control.
IM=Sluit|O=vertrouwelijke vensters|A=alstublieft|G=voordat u uw scherm deelt.
Please close confidential windows before sharing your screen.
A customer is about to share a screen for support. Ask formally that unrelated confidential windows be closed before sharing starts.
Voordat establishes a prerequisite. Close the windows does not mean delete their documents.
I can only see the window you are sharing.
During remote support, a customer asks what is visible to you. Explain formally that you can see only the shared window.
Alleen limits the visible scope. It does not claim that you can see the whole desktop.
I cannot control your computer through this connection.
A customer expects you to operate their device during a view-only call. Explain formally that this connection does not allow you to control it.
Niet kunnen describes technical capability here. It is distinct from not having permission to control the device.
I explain each action before you carry it out.
A customer is unsure how a remote support session will proceed. Explain formally that you will explain each action before they perform it.
Ze refers to de handeling. The customer performs the action; you explain it.
I ended screen sharing after the call.
A customer asks whether the screen remained shared after an earlier support call. Confirm formally that you ended sharing after the call.
The perfect reports termination of sharing, not deletion of a recording or account.
V=Ziet|S=u|O=de knop om het delen te stoppen?
Can you see the button to stop sharing?
During remote support, you want the customer to know how to end sharing. Ask formally whether they can see that button.
Dutch ziet u can ask about visibility without adding kunnen. Om te stoppen identifies the button's function.
What information may I view during this call?
Before viewing material in a support call, ask which information you are authorised to look at during that conversation.
Mag asks permission and scope. It does not claim technical ability to see material outside the shared window.
The user stopped screen sharing after the check.
A colleague asks how an earlier remote session ended. Report that the user stopped sharing the screen after the check.
The user is the person ending sharing. The past report does not imply that you stopped it remotely.
Can you share the correct window again?
A colleague accidentally stopped sharing the window relevant to a support check. Ask informally for that window to be shared again.
Nogmaals requests repetition of sharing. Juist identifies the intended window rather than every open window.
I will carry out the check together with you.
A customer is concerned about performing a check alone. Promise formally that you will work through it together.
Samen met u includes both participants; it does not transfer complete control to the support agent.
S=Ik|V=vraag|O=uw toestemming|TE=om de gedeelde gegevens te bekijken.
I am asking your permission to view the shared data.
During a support call, a customer's shared window contains relevant information. Ask formally for permission before viewing that data.
Toestemming om introduces the permitted action. Merely sharing a window is not presented as unlimited authorisation.
I am investigating the report, but I do not know the cause yet.
A customer asks why their issue occurs while your investigation is still underway. Explain formally that you are investigating but have not established the cause.
Ongoing investigation and established knowledge are different. Nog niet avoids inventing a diagnosis.
I cannot promise a solution today.
A customer asks for a guaranteed fix today, but you cannot commit to that. Explain formally that you cannot make that promise.
Cannot promise is not the same as refusing to investigate or predicting definite failure today.
S=Ik|MOD=zal|O=u|T=voor het einde van de dag|I=bijwerken|PP=over de voortgang.
I will update you on progress before the end of the day.
A customer needs a follow-up while the issue is investigated. Commit formally to providing a progress update before the day ends.
This promises an update, not necessarily a completed fix. Bijwerken with a person is less natural than op de hoogte brengen and will be reviewed.
I will let you know as soon as there is new information.
A customer asks when they will hear from you again. Promise formally to notify them when new information becomes available.
Zodra gives the trigger for contact. It does not promise a new diagnosis at a specific time.
S=De volgende stap|V=is|C=een controle van de instellingen.
The next step is a check of the settings.
A customer asks what will happen next in the investigation. Explain formally that the next action is to check the settings.
The check is a planned next step. It is not a claim that the settings have already been proved incorrect.
I have recorded the agreed follow-up in the ticket.
A colleague asks whether the customer follow-up arrangement is documented. Confirm that it has been recorded in the ticket.
Vastgelegd documents an agreement; it does not mean that the follow-up conversation has already occurred.
Can you continue working with the workaround in the meantime?
A permanent fix is not yet available. Ask the customer formally whether the proposed workaround lets them continue their work for now.
Ondertussen means in the meantime. A workaround is not described as a permanent repair.
Q=Welk onderdeel van uw werk|V=heeft|O=de meeste last van dit probleem?
Which part of your work is most affected by this problem?
You need to understand the customer's priorities while investigating. Ask formally which part of their work the problem affects most.
Last hebben van is a fixed expression. It describes impact rather than identifying a technical cause.
S=We|PAST=spraken|O=een update na de eerste controle|PART=af.
We agreed on an update after the first check.
A colleague asks what follow-up was promised to the customer. Report that an update was agreed after the first check.
Spraken af is plural past. An agreed update is not the same as a promised resolution.
S=Een duidelijke tussenstand|V=is|C=nuttiger dan een onbevestigde belofte.
A clear interim update is more useful than an unconfirmed promise.
A colleague is unsure what to tell a waiting user. Explain that a clear interim update is more useful than a promise nobody has confirmed.
The comparative contrasts communication choices; it does not discourage providing a confirmed resolution time when one is actually known.
S=Ik|V=noteer|O=uw belangrijkste vraag|TE=om de terugkoppeling daarop af te stemmen.
I am noting your main question so I can tailor the follow-up to it.
A customer has several concerns. Explain formally that you are recording their main question so the follow-up can address it directly.
Daarop refers to the main question. Af te stemmen is a separable te-infinitive.
V=Is|S=een update per e-mail|C=voor u voldoende?
Would an email update be sufficient for you?
You are agreeing a follow-up channel with a customer. Ask formally whether an email update would meet their needs.
Voldoende asks about sufficiency, not whether the issue is already resolved. Voor u is natural Belgian suitability wording.
V=Werkt|S=de toepassing|T=na de controle|C=weer zoals verwacht?
Does the application work as expected again after the check?
A customer has just repeated a check after support work. Ask whether the application's behaviour now meets their expectation.
This is a yes/no question. Weer asks about restored behaviour without claiming that the underlying cause is permanently removed.
A customer's immediate support request appears complete. Ask formally for agreement to close the report rather than assuming it can be closed.
Afsluiten means close the support record, not delete its history. Mag requests permission/agreement.
I have added your confirmation to the ticket.
A customer has confirmed the result of a support check. Tell them formally that you have added that confirmation to the ticket.
A recorded confirmation is distinct from deleting the ticket or automatically proving every aspect of a fix.
S=Het afsluiten van het ticket|V=verwijdert|O=de geschiedenis|NEG=niet.
Closing the ticket does not delete its history.
A customer worries that closing a support ticket erases the record. Explain formally that closing does not remove its history.
Het afsluiten is a nominalised infinitive inside the subject. The statement distinguishes closing from deletion.
S=Ik|V=laat|O=de melding|C=open|G=omdat de gebruiker nog niet heeft bevestigd.
I am leaving the report open because the user has not confirmed yet.
A colleague asks why you have not closed a support report. Explain that the user's confirmation is still missing.
Nog niet means not yet. Omdat gives the reason for keeping it open; it does not claim that the user rejected the result.
IM=Vermeld|O=het ticketnummer|G=als u hierover opnieuw contact opneemt.
Quote the ticket number if you contact us about this again.
You are finishing a support conversation with a customer. Ask formally that they mention the same ticket number if they contact support about this issue again.
Hierover refers back to the current issue. Contact opneemt is a final verb expression inside the conditional clause.
S=De gebruiker|V=bevestigt|G=dat de taak weer lukt.
The user confirms that the task works again.
A colleague asks what the user reported after a check. Say that the user confirms they can perform the task again.
The statement attributes the outcome to the user's confirmation, rather than making an unsupported universal guarantee.
After the final call I closed the report.
A colleague asks when you closed a completed support report. Say that you closed it after the final call.
Sloot ... af is simple past. Closing the report does not mean deleting it.
I will put the agreed follow-up care in the calendar.
A customer needs a planned check after the main support work. Promise formally to schedule the agreed follow-up care.
This is a scheduling commitment, not a statement that the follow-up check has already happened.
Do you have any further questions about the steps carried out?
You are ending a support appointment after performing several steps. Ask the customer formally whether they have further questions about those steps.
Nog asks for remaining questions. It does not presume that the customer has understood everything already.
S=Ik|V=beschrijf|O=het resultaat|TE=om een volgende opvolging gemakkelijker te maken.
I describe the result to make future follow-up easier.
A colleague asks why you are adding a final result note. Explain that recording the result will help with any later follow-up.
Om expresses documentation's purpose. Een volgende opvolging is potential future follow-up, not a promise that another issue will occur.
G=Als het probleem terugkomt,|V=kan|S=de gebruiker|PP=naar dit ticket|I=verwijzen.
If the problem returns, the user can refer to this ticket.
You are briefing a colleague before closing a report. Explain that the user can refer to the same ticket if the problem recurs.
Als is conditional; this does not predict a recurrence. Verwijzen naar identifies the reference record.
